```{r}
#1- loading data, look at data set up way to clean
library(tidyverse)
covar <- read_csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")        
expr  <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
gene <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")

#view(covar)
#view(expr)
#view(gene)


##first col of expr has empty name, covar: description with data, remove those 
##and better label

##expr first col rename to ProbID
expr <- expr %>% rename(ProbID = 1)

##Cleaning covar so that there is no description, col have right value type, 
clean_covar <- covar %>%
  mutate(across(-c(subjectID, geoID), ~ str_remove(.x, "^.*?:\\s*"))) %>%
  mutate(
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(mat_age_yrs),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(delivery_gestAge_wks),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks),
    mat_BMI = as.numeric(mat_BMI),
    mat_vitD = as.numeric(mat_vitD),
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia, levels = c("Normal",
                                                             "Preeclampsia")),
    mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, levels = c("0", "1"),labels = c("Healthy",
                        "Asthma")), batch_Microarray = factor(batch_Microarray)
  ) %>%

## Gene:TMEM176B
  #Continuous covariate: VitD
  #Categorical 1: age_group
  #Categorical 2: preeclampsia
  # Derive a categorical variable from a continuous one (Age-group/maternal age)
  mutate(age_group = factor(
  ifelse(mat_age_yrs < 25, "<25",
         ifelse(mat_age_yrs < 30, "25-29", "30+")),
  levels = c("<25", "25-29", "30+")))

#view(clean_covar)
#connect probID to gene so that I can now specify my gene of interest

## expression file has probe ID but no gene names, gene file pairs probe ID 
##with gene name. Use left join to combine these two tables. The column names 
##are different so have to tell r they are actually the same info. To make 
##easier to read use relocate to move the new gene column next to probe id. 
##Check to make sure every probe found a match

expr_named <- expr %>%
  left_join(gene, by =c("ProbID" = "PROBEID")) %>%
  relocate(GENE, .after = ProbID)
sum(is.na(expr_named$GENE)) 

#assigning my gene of interest
my_gene <- "TMEM176B"


##I have my gene now I need to figure out where it is in the table. reshape 
##table into two columns that I can merge on my covariates. Dont need the 
##probID or gene columns. I also want my gene names to be rows so I have to 
##pivot_longer.

gene_long <- expr_named %>%
  filter(GENE == my_gene) %>%
  select(-ProbID, -GENE) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "geoID", values_to = "expression")

#save pivot table to dat
dat <- gene_long %>%
  inner_join(clean_covar, by = "geoID")

## Checking data to make sure nothing was lost and everything matches correctly.

## Count the rows in merged data, does sample Id in covariate file appear as a 
## col name in expression file, does every sample col in expression file appear 
## in covariate file (except for first column), ask if expression values are 
## missing, and count how many samples fall into each combination of 
## preeclampsia status and age group

nrow(dat)                                    
all(clean_covar$geoID %in% names(expr))      
all(names(expr)[-1] %in% clean_covar$geoID)  
anyNA(dat$expression)                        
table(dat$preg_preeclampsia, dat$age_group) 


#Setting theme and colors
theme_1 <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "right")

pe_colors <- c("Normal" = "#A888B5", "Preeclampsia" = "#EC5353")


#Histogram of gene expression
p_hist <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#A888B5", color = "black") +
  labs(title = paste(my_gene, "Expression Distribution"),
       x = paste(my_gene, "Expression Level"),
       y = "Number of samples") +
  theme_1

p_hist
#saving plot as pdf for presentations
ggsave("sub1_plots_hist1.pdf")

# scatter plot vitD vs expression
p_scatter <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "#A888B5") +
  labs(title = paste(my_gene, "Expression vs. Maternal Vitamin D"),
       x = "Maternal vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D, ng/mL)",
       y = paste(my_gene, "Expression Level")) +
  theme_1

p_scatter
#saving plot as pdf for presentations
ggsave("sub1_plots_scatter_1.pdf")
# Boxplot preeclampsia vs age group
p_box <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = age_group, y = expression,
                         fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pe_colors, name = "Pregnancy outcome") +
  labs(title = paste(my_gene,
                     "Expression by Age Group\n and Preeclampsia status"),
       x = "Maternal age group (years)",
       y = paste(my_gene, "Expression Level")) +
  theme_1

p_box
#saving plot as pdf for presentations
ggsave("sub1_plots.pdf")

# used material from other classes (Data wrangling and Biostat) and AI for debugging
```

```{r}
#Start of submission2

#need somewhere to store my genes
my_genes <- c("TMEM176B", "UTS2", "CLIC2")

#need a table with one row per sample and one column per gene.
genes_wide <- expr_named %>%
  filter(GENE %in% my_genes)%>%
  select(-ProbID)%>%
  pivot_longer(-GENE, names_to = "geoID", values_to = "expression") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = GENE, values_from = expression)

#each gene name becomes its own column,filled with the genes expression values.(merging genes_wide with vitD, age group etc.)

dat_all <- genes_wide %>%
  inner_join(clean_covar, by = "geoID")

#check to make sure it includes genes (it is)
##nrow(dat_all)
##names(dat_all)

#make theme for plots based on prof.comment in submission 1 (added more x/y ticks in histogram and scatter plot)
  legible_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      axis.title   = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text    = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    )



#making function:
# wants function to make histogram, scatter plot and boxplot for each gene. for each gene in list, copy genes column into new col, plot histogram, plot scatter plot, plot boxplot, call function to dat_all and specify genes (my_genes) 


make_gene_plots <- function(df, genes) {
  

  for (g in genes) {

    # copy this gene's values into a column called "expression"
    df$expression <- df[[g]]

    # Histogram of expression
    print(ggplot(df, aes(x = expression)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#A888B5", color = "white") +
      labs(title = paste(g, "Expression Distribution"),
           x = paste(g, "Expression Level"),
           y = "Number of samples")+
        scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
        scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
        legible_theme)
   
    # Scatterplot: vitamin D vs expression
    print(ggplot(df, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "#A888B5") +
      labs(title = str_wrap(paste(g, "Expression vs. Maternal VitaminD"), width = 40),
           x = "Maternal vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D, ng/mL)",
           y = paste(g, "Expression Level"))+
        scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
        scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
        legible_theme)

    # Boxplot: age group and preeclampsia status
    print(ggplot(df, aes(x = age_group, y = expression, fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
      geom_boxplot() +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("#A888B5", "#EC5353"), name = "Pregnancy outcome") +
      labs(title = str_wrap(paste(g, "Expression by Age Group and Preeclampsia Status"),
                            width = 40),
           x = "Maternal age group (years)",
           y = paste(g, "Expression Level"))+
        # tried to do geom_jitter but it didn't look right, so i had to look up an alternative
       geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
             size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE)+
        legible_theme)
    
  }
  
}

# call it
make_gene_plots(dat_all, my_genes)

#used AI and google to look specific things up that I forgot or to debugg.
```

```{r}
#Submission 3--> summary statistics table
#install.packages("tableone")
library(tableone)

#Create a table one looking at Maternal Vit.D, BMI, Gestational age (continuous)
#Preeclampsia status and Maternal age group (categorical)

#only want to select variables and make the labels readaale
table_1 <- clean_covar %>%
  select(preg_preeclampsia, mat_vitD, mat_BMI, delivery_gestAge_wks,
         age_group) %>%
  rename(`Maternal vitamin D (ng/mL)`             = mat_vitD,
         `Maternal BMI (kg/m2)`                   = mat_BMI,
         `Gestational age at delivery (weeks)`    = delivery_gestAge_wks,
         `Maternal age group (years)`             = age_group)

#every column except the grouping variable
vars_all <- table_1 %>% select(-preg_preeclampsia) %>% names()

tab1 <- CreateTableOne(vars = vars_all,
                       strata = "preg_preeclampsia",
                       data = table_1,
                       factorVars = "Maternal age group (years)")

tab1
#use Tables generator link from class to turn into LaTex form
#Used suggested table one package from class
```

```{r}
#Making Heat map. Select 10 genes: FIG4, CNR1, BRDT, CA3, SIRT3, JAK2, LHB, TMEM176B, UTS2, CLIC2

heat_genes <- c("FIG4","CNR1","BRDT","CA3","SIRT3","JAK2","LHB","TMEM176B","UTS2", "CLIC2")

library(pheatmap)

#filter only the 10 genes I want from the expression table
#calculate variance for each row
heat_df <- expr_named %>%
  filter(GENE %in% heat_genes) %>%
  mutate(row_var = apply(as.matrix(across(all_of(clean_covar$geoID))), 1, var)) %>%
  group_by(GENE) %>%
  slice(match(heat_genes, GENE))

#from what I understand heat map needs a matrix so convert dataset to matrix and have gene names as row
heat_mat <- as.matrix(heat_df[, clean_covar$geoID])
rownames(heat_mat) <- heat_df$GENE

#Checking dimensions
#dim(heat_mat)                

#Need annotation bars above the heatmap so specify and specify the colors to use
annot_col <- data.frame(Outcome   = clean_covar$preg_preeclampsia,
                        Age_group = clean_covar$age_group,
                        row.names = clean_covar$geoID)

annot_colors <- list(
  Outcome   = c("Normal" = "#A888B5", "Preeclampsia" = "#EC5353"),
  Age_group = c("<25" = "#E69F00", "25-29" = "#56B4E9", "30+" = "#009E73")
)

#Create a function so to create the heatmap, clustering has to be complete (linking for hierarchial clustering)
draw_heatmap <- function(mat, annot, annot_cols) {
  pheatmap(heat_mat,
           scale = "row",                  
           clustering_method = "complete",
           annotation_col = annot_col,
           annotation_colors = annot_colors,
           show_colnames = FALSE,         
           fontsize_row = 11,
           main = "Expression of 10 selected genes",
           filename= "heatmap.png")
}

draw_heatmap(mat, annot, annot_cols)

#had to look up how to save a pheatmap so added filename after. 

```

```{r}
# ridgeline plot aka joyplot which shows overall distribution 
#install.packages("ggridges")
library(ggridges)

#pivot longer to turn the three gene columns into two columns
#Looked up format and modified to my own data, inputs
#aes: one ridge per gene, fill = two overlapping curves per gene, alpha = make transparent so overlap is visible 

p_ridge <- dat_all %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(my_genes), names_to = "gene", values_to = "expression") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = expression, y = gene, fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.7, scale = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pe_colors, name = "Pregnancy outcome") +
  labs(title = "Gene Expression by Preeclampsia Status",
       x = "Expression level", y = NULL) +
  legible_theme

p_ridge
ggsave("ridges.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
#organizing graphs for paper, had to look up how to display ggplot graphs in one go, also had to look up how to insert the a/b/c

#install.packages("patchwork")
library(patchwork)

#Use lapply to build one plot per gene and store them in list (instead of printing above)
#Use patchwork to combine each list into one figure
#Each function has to copy the genes column and turn into generic expression column so that the same ggplot code could work for every gene

#histogram

hist_plots <- lapply(my_genes, function(g) {
  df <- dat_all
  df$expression <- df[[g]]

  ggplot(df, aes(x = expression)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#A888B5", color = "white") +
    labs(title = paste(g, "Expression Distribution"),
         x = paste(g, "Expression Level"),
         y = "Number of samples") +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
    scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
    legible_theme
})
#scatterplot: gene expression vs maternal vitamin D
#titles were long so I had to look up how to fix that and found str_wrap which splits long titles into two lines so they dont get cut off
scatter_plots <- lapply(my_genes, function(g) {
  df <- dat_all
  df$expression <- df[[g]]

  ggplot(df, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "#A888B5") +
    labs(title = str_wrap(paste(g, "Expression vs. Maternal VitaminD"), width = 40),
         x = "Maternal vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D, ng/mL)",
         y = paste(g, "Expression Level")) +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
    scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
    legible_theme
})

#Boxplot: 
box_plots <- lapply(my_genes, function(g) {
  df <- dat_all
  df$expression <- df[[g]]

  ggplot(df, aes(x = age_group, y = expression, fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#A888B5", "#EC5353"), name = "Pregnancy outcome") +
    labs(title = str_wrap(paste(g, "Expression by Age Group and Preeclampsia Status"),
                          width = 40),
         x = "Maternal age group (years)",
         y = paste(g, "Expression Level")) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
               size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
    legible_theme
})

# I want 3 figures, 3 panels each, with a, b, c labels
#Looks squished, so had to look up a way to fix, tested with ggsave and specified height, width and dpi which worked out even though it still looks squished here.

wrap_plots(hist_plots, ncol = 3) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
ggsave("figure_hist.png", width = 18, height = 6, dpi = 300)

wrap_plots(scatter_plots, ncol = 3) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
ggsave("figure_scatter.png", width = 18, height = 6, dpi = 300)

wrap_plots(box_plots, ncol = 3) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
ggsave("figure_box.png", width = 18, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
